lines.text: Some ancient people brushed their teeth with urine.
And in Rome, it gets weirder. Wait for the end.
Over two thousand years ago, a Roman poet mocked a man for his gleaming teeth.
lines.caption: Over 2,000 years ago, a Roman poet mocked a man for his gleaming teeth.

lines.text: His joke? The man rinsed them with urine, a habit blamed on ancient Spain.
Romans used urine too. Laundry workers used its ammonia to whiten wool togas.
It was so valuable, Emperor Vespasian taxed it.
When his son complained, he held a tax coin to his son's nose. Smell anything? Money doesn't stink.
Sounds fake? It's true. Follow for more.
